modules.title: A Quick Overview of Web Development
modules.bigIdea: Every website is a conversation between a browser and a server. Knowing who does what is the foundation for every decision you make when you build a page.
modules.overview: Before writing a single tag, you need a mental map of the territory. This module shows how a web page travels from a server to your screen, where HTML, CSS and JavaScript fit, and how to set up your working studio.
learningOutcomes: Explain how a browser and a server exchange a web page.
Describe the different jobs of HTML, CSS and JavaScript.
Distinguish client-side tasks from server-side tasks.
Name common technologies used to build and deliver websites.
modules.projectThread: Set up your studio and trace a web request: install VS Code, create my-first-site, open Network tab on 3 sites, write a web map, and choose the website idea you will build throughout the course.
modules.buildGoal: Understand how the web works and set up your tools.

lessons.title: HTML is Part of a Team

modules.title: Introduction to HTML
modules.bigIdea: A web page is just a text file with meaning added. Learn the skeleton once and you can build any page on the internet.
modules.overview: Write your first real page: elements, tags, attributes, comments, the fixed skeleton every page needs, whitespace, special characters, and a short history of HTML.
learningOutcomes: Understand how whitespace is treated in HTML.
Add special characters to HTML pages.
Explain the general history of HTML.
modules.projectThread: Your 'About Me' home page: create index.html with full skeleton, lang="en", heading with your name, copyright line, and at least three comments. Compare View Source with a professional site.

lessons.title: Getting Started with a Simple HTML Document

modules.title: Paragraphs, Headings, and Text
modules.bigIdea: Good web writing is structured writing. Headings, paragraphs and emphasis tell both people and machines what matters on the page.
modules.overview: Organise written content with paragraphs and heading levels, control breaks, quote sources, display code with pre, and mark up words by meaning (semantic HTML).
learningOutcomes: Use phrase elements to call out or identify textual elements.
Understand the meaning of semantic content.
modules.projectThread: Write a real article (300–500 words) with one h1, three h2 sections, a blockquote, pre sample, time element, and proper inline semantics. Read the headings alone — do they tell the story?

modules.title: HTML Links
modules.bigIdea: Links are what make the web a web. Every journey across a site, and between sites, is a link someone chose to place.
modules.overview: Connect pages together: absolute vs relative paths, new tabs safely, email links, and jump to specific places within a long page.
learningOutcomes: Explain the difference between absolute and relative paths.
Add links that open in new tabs or windows.
Add links that open an email client.
Add links to specific locations on a page.
modules.projectThread: Connect your site: three pages with shared navigation, one page in a subfolder with fixed relative paths, table of contents with anchors, external link with rel=noopener, and a mailto link.

lessons.title: Linking to a Specific Location on the Page
Targeting a Specific Location on the Page

modules.title: HTML Images
modules.bigIdea: Images carry emotion, but they must also be fast, accessible and meaningful to everyone, including people who cannot see them.
modules.overview: Insert images responsibly: formats, dimensions, image links, alternative text, figure/figcaption, and the first steps of image performance.
learningOutcomes: Add images to an HTML page.
Make images accessible with appropriate alternative text.
modules.projectThread: A gallery with a story: six optimised images with meaningful alt text and captions, logo as home link, test a broken path to see alt text in action.

lessons.title: Exercise: Adding Images to the Page

modules.title: HTML Lists
modules.bigIdea: Lists organise information so people can scan it. They are also the hidden structure behind almost every menu on the web.
modules.overview: Three list types, nesting, and how lists become building blocks for menus once CSS arrives.
modules.projectThread: A recipe or how-to page: unordered list for materials, ordered list for steps, definition list for glossary, one nested list, and convert navigation into a ul inside nav.

modules.title: Crash Course in CSS
modules.bigIdea: CSS turns a plain document into a designed experience. One stylesheet can change the look of a whole website in seconds.
modules.overview: The largest module: rules, selectors, cascade, resets, units, media types, viewport, inheritance, and attaching styles three ways.
learningOutcomes: Explain the role of CSS resets and normalizers.
Create and use external and embedded stylesheets.
Add inline styles to HTML elements.
Understand and use the viewport meta tag.
Understand and select appropriate units of measurement.
modules.projectThread: Give your site an identity: create css/style.css with a reset, horizontal nav with hover, card component, print rule, and inspect one overridden rule in DevTools.
modules.buildGoal: A designed site with a reusable stylesheet.

modules.title: CSS Fonts
modules.bigIdea: Typography is where a site gains its voice. The right font choices make a page feel warm, serious, playful or trustworthy before anyone reads a word.
modules.overview: Control typeface, size, weight, spacing and custom fonts. Build a consistent type scale.
modules.projectThread: A type system for your blog: heading + body fonts with fallbacks, size scale, comfortable line-height, optional @font-face, and print comparison.

modules.title: Color and Opacity
modules.bigIdea: Colour sets mood, guides attention and, when chosen well, makes a page usable by everyone.
modules.overview: Named colours, hex, rgb, hsl, opacity vs rgba, contrast ratios, and a small consistent palette.
modules.projectThread: Your brand palette: primary, accent, dark text, light background, neutral grey in hex and hsl. Apply to body, links, buttons. Check contrast ≥ 4.5:1.
modules.buildGoal: A brand palette that passes contrast checks.

lessons.title: Exercise: Adding Color and Opacity to Text

modules.title: CSS Text
modules.bigIdea: Once fonts and colours are set, text properties shape rhythm, alignment and emphasis — where reading becomes pleasant.
modules.overview: letter-spacing, text-align, decoration, indent, shadow, transform, white-space, word-break and word-spacing.
modules.projectThread: Polish a hero and an article: uppercase letter-spaced headline with shadow, comfortable line length (~65ch), proper long-URL wrapping on mobile.

modules.title: JavaScript Basics
modules.bigIdea: JavaScript turns pages into programs. With a few lines you can respond to people, change what they see and make the page feel alive.
modules.overview: JavaScript vs ECMAScript, the DOM, syntax, finding elements, where scripts live, objects/methods/properties, and your first interactive touches.
learningOutcomes: Understand the HTML Document Object Model.
Work with JavaScript objects, methods, and properties.
modules.projectThread: Make your site respond: external js/main.js with defer, button that changes theme, greeting on load, document.title change, deliberate error then fix.
modules.buildGoal: Interactive touches that respond to visitors.

lessons.title: Exercise: Alerts, Writing, and Changing Background Color

capstone.title: Build Your Meaningful Website
capstone.description: Your capstone is the website you have been growing since Module 1. It should have a clear purpose, a real audience and content that you care about.
purposes: Personal portfolio — introduce yourself, show your work, make contact easy
Hobby or knowledge blog — teach something you love
Small business or service page — explain what you offer with a gallery
Community or cause site — share an event, story or campaign

requirements.items: Valid skeleton, language set, one h1 per page, logical heading outline, semantic inline text
Consistent list-based menu, working relative paths, anchors, email link
At least five optimised images, meaningful alt text, one image link, captions
External stylesheet, contrast-checked palette, type scale, card/hero, viewport, print rule
External script with defer that changes something visible and logs to the console
Tested in two browsers and mobile preview, no broken links, no console errors
